items.stem: Why does delivering work in small, frequent increments reduce project risk?

options.text: Feedback arrives sooner, so wrong assumptions are caught early
options.rationale: Correct: short feedback loops surface problems before they compound.

options.text: It removes the need to prioritise
options.rationale: Increments still require prioritisation of what to build first.

options.text: It guarantees the project finishes faster
options.rationale: It reduces risk and enables adaptation, but does not guarantee speed.

options.text: It means documentation is never needed
options.rationale: Agile values working output but does not forbid documentation.

items.explanation: Correct: short feedback loops surface problems before they compound.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which statements about a product backlog are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: It is ordered, typically with the highest-value items near the top
options.rationale: Correct: a backlog is prioritised so the most valuable work is done first.

options.text: It can change as the team learns more
options.rationale: Correct: the backlog is refined and reordered over time.

options.text: It must be fully fixed before any work starts
options.rationale: Agile expects the backlog to evolve, not be frozen up front.

options.text: Items are always worked in the order they were requested
options.rationale: Order is by value and risk, not request sequence.

items.explanation: Correct: a backlog is prioritised so the most valuable work is done first.

items.stem: A team holds all the Scrum ceremonies but never changes anything based on the retrospective. What anti-pattern is this?

options.text: Agile in name only - practising ceremonies without inspect-and-adapt
options.rationale: Correct: following rituals without acting on learning is 'agile in name only'.
The issue is failing to improve, not prioritisation.
Frequent delivery is desirable; the gap is not acting on retrospectives.
Safety is not the problem described here.

items.explanation: Correct: following rituals without acting on learning is 'agile in name only'.
